Custom predictive performance statistic

Source: R/custom_stat.R
custom_stat.Rd

Defines a predictive performance statistic (a utility or a loss) from a user function. Use the result in argument stats of summary.vsel(), plot.vsel() and performances(), or in argument stat of suggest_size(). The statistic affects the evaluation of the submodels and the suggested size, but not the search.

Usage

custom_stat(
  fun,
  name,
  type = c("pointwise", "aggregate"),
  higher_better = TRUE,
  label = name
)

Arguments

fun

A function with arguments y, mu and wobs (see section "Details").

name

A single character string. The output of summary.vsel() and performances() uses it in the column names and adds suffixes such as .se, so it must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores. It must not be the name of a built-in statistic or of another column of these tables ("size", "ranking_fulldata", "cv_proportions_diag").

type

Either "pointwise" or "aggregate" (see section "Details").

higher_better

TRUE for a utility (higher values are better), FALSE for a loss. baseline = "best" and suggest_size() use it.

label

A single character string for the facet label in plot.vsel().

Value

An object of class custom_stat.

Details

Function fun gets these arguments for each model (the reference model and each submodel size):

  • y: the observed response values of the evaluation (test) set. For the binomial() family, y holds the proportions of successes (the number of successes divided by the number of trials). For the latent projection, y holds the response values on the original response scale if resp_oscale = TRUE and the latent response values if resp_oscale = FALSE.

  • mu: the predictive means for the observations in y, averaged over the parameter draws of the reference model or over the projected draws of the submodel. For the binomial() family, these are the predicted probabilities of success. With cross-validation, mu holds the cross-validated predictions. For the latent projection, mu is on the same scale as y. mu can contain NAs. With subsampled LOO CV (see argument nloo of cv_varsel()), the submodel predictions are NA for the observations outside the subsample. For a reference model of class datafit, all reference model predictions are NA.

  • wobs: the observation weights (for the binomial() family: the number of trials).

For type = "pointwise", fun returns a numeric (or logical) vector of the same length as y with the utility (or loss) of each observation. Element i must depend only on y[i], mu[i] and wobs[i]. Do not apply wobs in fun: the statistic is the mean of these values, weighted by wobs. As for "mse", the standard error treats each row of the evaluation set as one observation. For the binomial() family, a row with several trials thus counts once, whereas "acc" splits it into single trials. The difference from the baseline model pairs the two models observation by observation. The uncertainty intervals use a normal approximation. Subsampled LOO CV works with this type.

For type = "aggregate", fun returns a single number for the whole evaluation set. As for "auc", the standard error and the uncertainty intervals come from a bootstrap over the rows of the evaluation set (see argument ... of summary.vsel() for the number of bootstrap samples and the seed). The difference from the baseline model uses the same bootstrap samples for both models. For the binomial() family, a row with several trials counts once, whereas "auc" splits it into single trials. This type does not support subsampled LOO CV.

Custom statistics are not available for the augmented-data projection, or for the latent projection with resp_oscale = TRUE and a non-NULL element family$cats.

Examples

# Net benefit at the decision threshold `thres` (a utility). Each observation
# contributes one pointwise term:
net_benefit <- function(thres) {
  custom_stat(
    function(y, mu, wobs) {
      treat <- mu >= thres
      treat * (y - (1 - y) * thres / (1 - thres))
    },
    name = paste0("nb", 100 * thres),
    label = paste0("Net benefit \u2265 ", thres)
  )
}

# Data:
dat_binom <- data.frame(y = df_binom$y, df_binom$x)

# The `stanreg` fit which will be used as the reference model (with small
# values for `chains` and `iter`, but only for technical reasons in this
# example; this is not recommended in general):
fit <- rstanarm::stan_glm(
  y ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5, family = binomial(), data = dat_binom,
  chains = 2, iter = 500, refresh = 0, seed = 9876
)

# Run varsel() (here without cross-validation and with small values for
# `nterms_max` and `nclusters_pred`, but only for the sake of speed in this
# example; this is not recommended in general):
vs <- varsel(fit, nterms_max = 3, nclusters_pred = 10, seed = 5555)
print(summary(vs, stats = list("elpd", net_benefit(0.2))), digits = 2)
#>

#> Link function: logit 
#>

#> Projection method: traditional
